headline: Korean employers are increasingly naming specific AI tools in job ads, and mentions of Anthropic's Claude grew faster than any other tool in the third quarter, according to JobKorea.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: fresh data with clear figures, but it comes from one job site's own listings and counts mentions, not hires.
importance_line: What changed is that Korean employers now ask for named AI tools rather than general AI knowledge, which matters first to job seekers and workers in marketing, sales and operations, then to employers, but the figures are JobKorea's own and count mentions in postings, not jobs filled or tools actually used.
summary: The Korea Times reports, citing data released on 12 Oct 2026 by JobKorea, a Korean job platform run by Worksphere, that job postings naming AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini rose 170 percent in the third quarter from a year earlier, with mentions of Claude, the AI assistant made by Anthropic, up 770 percent. Claude now appears in 55 percent of postings that name a specific AI tool, up from 17 percent, against about 70 percent for ChatGPT, while mentions of Microsoft Word fell 16 percent.
notes: Full text read on the AMP page of The Korea Times. Figures are JobKorea's (Worksphere) own; the Korea Times says the article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by its staff. Printed link is the AMP page we read.
